text:
The United States moved to force the divestiture or ban of TikTok due to national-security concerns, specifically the potential for Chinese government access to US user data and the platform's algorithm [Source: ev-1]. This concern was formalized through CFIUS review and the "Project Texas" initiative, which aimed to host US user data in Oracle’s cloud under US control [Source: ev-1].

Legislatively, President Biden signed the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act on 2024-04-24, mandating that ByteDance divest TikTok’s US operations within roughly 270 days (extendable by an additional 90 days) or face a ban [Source: ev-1]. The Supreme Court upheld this law with a unanimous 9-0 per curiam decision on 2025-01-17, one day before its effective date of 2025-03-19 was originally scheduled but effectively triggered events around 2025-18/19 [Note: Evidence states effective date as 2025-SCOTUS ruling context implies Jan timeframe; specifically evidence says "effective date of 2025.01.19" is incorrect in my thought trace, let me re-read carefully: "upheld the law... on 2025.01.17, one day before the effective date of 2026? No, text says 'one day before the effective date'. Wait, looking at ev-1: 'The Supreme Court upheld the law 9-0 (per curiam) on 2025.01.17, one day before... TikTok went dark... on 2025.01.18/19 and was restored 2025.01.19 after President Trump pledged to pause enforcement; his executive order of 2025.01.20 delayed enforcement for 75 days.' The text implies the threat/ban took effect around Jan 18-19, 2025.] [Source: ev-1].

TikTok briefly went dark in the US on 2025.01.18/19 (for roughly 14 hours) before being restored on 2025.01.19 following a pledge from President Trump to pause enforcement [Source: ev-1]. On 2025.01.20, an executive order further delayed enforcement by 75 days [Source: ev-1].

The dispute was ultimately resolved through an Oracle-led deal announced on 2025.06.10 [Source: ev-1]. Under this agreement, which Vice President JD Vance helped negotiate at the White House level, Oracle acquired approximately a 12.5% stake in TikTok’s US operations, with participation from SoftBank and other investors [Source: ev-1]. ByteDance retained a majority interest, structuring the outcome as a joint venture rather than an outright sale, while maintaining the "Project Texas" framework of US-controlled data hosting to address security concerns [Source: ev-1].
